nodes.label: Connected Claude (MCP client)
nodes.description: A Claude session across the process boundary that speaks MCP to POST /mcp over streamable HTTP. It is the consumer of the es-view read surface: it calls get_node / get_flow / list_model / list_data_model and reads the event-storming://selected-nodes resource to ground a refactor in the live model. (get_current_selection is the same client's selection-aware read, owned by a sibling trace.) The @modelcontextprotocol/sdk used server-side is an in-process LIBRARY, not this external system.

tactical.explanation: SESSION TRANSPORT (plumbing, kept in tactical per the two-plane rule): createMcpHandler holds a `transports` Map keyed by Mcp-Session-Id. An `initialize` POST with no session id spins up a StreamableHTTPServerTransport (randomUUID sessionIdGenerator, enableJsonResponse) and connects a FRESH McpServer (buildMcpServer) that closes over the shared `services` + session (selection, bundle); onsessioninitialized registers the transport. Later POST/GET/DELETE reuse it by session id; transport.onclose deletes the session. Request bodies are capped at 4MB (readJsonBody destroys the socket past 4_000_000 bytes). Unknown node/flow ids come back as a plain text result (not an MCP protocol error) so the client can recover without a retry loop. RESOLVED: the pre-refactor mcp.mjs header comment called the transport 'stateless', contradicting the stateful per-session implementation and mcp.md. The refactored mcp-server.ts header comment drops that claim entirely, and its createMcpHandler JSDoc plainly states 'Stateful over streamable HTTP' — the old contradiction is gone.

anchors.note: transports Map keyed by Mcp-Session-Id
initialize => new StreamableHTTPServerTransport + fresh McpServer over shared services/selection/bundle
no longer claims 'stateless'; createMcpHandler JSDoc (mcp-server.ts:111) now says 'Stateful over streamable HTTP' — the old contradiction with mcp.md is resolved

nodes.label: The Model
nodes.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): the deduped node set plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta. Built by the merge, then held in memory by the es-view server. Its invariants are the merge-time validations. On this read path it is a read-only source: every MCP projection looks nodes/flows up in it, nothing writes it.

tactical.explanation: READ SIDE (this flow): buildServices resolves the model once at boot into `services` = { model, indexes: buildIndexes(model), repoRoot, comments, readSource }, shared same-process by the JSON API and the MCP tools. list_model iterates model.flows/model.nodes; buildNodeContext/buildFlowContext look up indexes.nodeById and derive fields/breadcrumb/usedBy/storage/enforces/flows via selectors; renderDataModelMarkdown walks the physical nodes via dataModelTree. No write occurs on the read path. Because services is built once, the read tools always project the boot-time model snapshot.

anchors.note: model + buildIndexes(model) + repoRoot + comments + readSource shared by API and MCP
reads indexes.nodeById + selectors to ground a node

nodes.label: Curated context bundle
nodes.description: The insertion-ordered set of typed refs { type: 'node' | 'flow' | 'hotspot', id } the human has gathered in the explorer (right-click, 'Add to context bundle'). Purely in-memory session state; the read half consumed by the selected-nodes MCP resource. Shares one createState() closure with the current selection (agg-selection); modeled as a distinct aggregate here because the resource reads only the bundle.

tactical.explanation: ContextBundle (its own class) holds a private `bundle` Map keyed by `type:id`. Written by the SPA via the addContextItem/removeContextItem application commands (POST/DELETE /api/context) and READ here by the selected-nodes resource callback via bundle.list(), which returns the typed refs in insertion order. Non-persistent by design; lost when the process exits. It is now a standalone class, separate from Selection — the two used to share one createState() closure; they no longer do.

anchors.note: insertion-ordered typed refs returned to the resource
in-memory bundle Map, own class — no longer shares Selection's closure

nodes.label: Model index
nodes.description: A compact index of the whole model: every flow id + name (+ status tag when not live), and every node id + label + type. The discovery surface Claude uses to find ids for get_node / get_flow. Returned by list_model. A pure in-memory projection: it does NOT ground source.

tactical.explanation: The list_model MCP tool handler (mcp-server.ts:70) delegates to the listModel query (application/queries/list-model.ts:5), which maps model.flows to `- \`id\` — name [status?]` and model.nodes to `- \`id\` — label _(type)_`, joins them under 'Flows (n)' / 'Nodes (n)' headings, and returns the markdown as an MCP text result. Straight iteration over agg-model; no readSource, no filesystem touch.

anchors.note: registerTool: empty inputSchema
map model.flows + model.nodes into a compact id index

nodes.label: Grounded node context
nodes.description: The full grounded context for any node id: type, description, conceptual fields with lineage, physical breadcrumb / contained fields / consumers / storage links, the invariant enforces-relation (aggregate/invariant only), the flows it appears in, human comments, and every source anchor with a real code excerpt. Returned by get_node; the same projection backs the SPA detail panel.

tactical.explanation: get_node(nodeId) (zod string arg, mcp-server.ts:43) delegates to the getNode query (application/queries/get-node.ts:5), which calls buildNodeContext(services, nodeId): looks up indexes.nodeById (agg-model); if missing, returns 'Unknown node — use list_model'. Otherwise maps fields (resolving each source ref to its physical node), derives breadcrumb/contained/usedBy/storage via selectors, computes enforcesRelation and nodeFlows, attaches services.comments.get('node', id) (empty when no comment store is wired), and for EVERY anchor pulls a repo-sandboxed source excerpt via services.readSource(repoRoot, path, line) (default true). renderNodeContextMarkdown formats it, fenced code included.

anchors.note: registerTool: nodeId string; delegates to the getNode query
buildNodeContext -> renderNodeContextMarkdown
fields/breadcrumb/contained/usedBy/storage/enforces/flows/comments/anchors
markdown projection incl. fenced source code

nodes.label: Grounded flow (with Mermaid graph)
nodes.description: A whole flow grounded in code: trigger/summary, the edges as labeled verbs, hotspots (open questions), every node grounded with source excerpts, and a Mermaid flowchart colored by the event-storming palette so the model sees the graph structurally (exact labels, no OCR). Returned by get_flow. Note: the Mermaid graph is a documented feature (mcp.md) that the tool's own registered description omits.

tactical.explanation: get_flow(flowId) (zod string arg, mcp-server.ts:53) delegates to the getFlow query (application/queries/get-flow.ts:5), which calls buildFlowContext(services, flowId): finds the flow in model.flows (agg-model); if missing, returns 'Unknown flow — use list_model'. Otherwise grounds each node id via buildNodeContext (-> readSource excerpts), maps edges to { from,to,verb,fromLabel,toLabel }, resolves hotspots via indexes.hotspotById, and builds a colored Mermaid flowchart via flowMermaid. renderFlowMarkdown assembles trigger/summary/edges/hotspots/mermaid/nodes.

anchors.note: registerTool: flowId string; delegates to the getFlow query
buildFlowContext -> renderFlowMarkdown
grounds every node + edges + hotspots + Mermaid
palette-colored Mermaid flowchart of the flow graph

nodes.label: Recovered data model
nodes.description: The physical storage the code actually touches, as a containment tree (server ▸ database ▸ table ▸ column, or filesystem ▸ directory ▸ file, or broker ▸ queue ▸ field — whatever storeKind fits), and for each record set the behavioral nodes that write/read/project it. Answers 'what tables does this touch / where does this data live / who writes this'. Returned by list_data_model; also the Data-model tab. Pure projection over agg-model, no source grounding.

tactical.explanation: list_data_model (mcp-server.ts:73) delegates to the listDataModel query (application/queries/list-data-model.ts:5), which calls renderDataModelMarkdown(services): dataModelTree(model, nodeById) folds the datastore/field nodes into a containment forest (storage-neutral, driven by parent pointers and storeKind), and for each record-set datastore (isRecordSet) datastoreConsumers lists the behavioral nodes + verb. Returns a 'run the data-mapping phase' placeholder when no datastore/field nodes exist. The registered tool description is relational-worded ('servers ▸ databases ▸ tables ▸ columns') whereas the implementation is storage-neutral.

anchors.note: registerTool -> delegates to the listDataModel query
renderDataModelMarkdown(services)
dataModelTree walk + per-record-set consumers
storage-neutral containment forest from parent pointers

nodes.label: Local filesystem
nodes.description: The local filesystem outside the process, reached through node:fs. On this read path it is the source of the REAL code excerpts each grounded projection pulls behind an anchor (the repo source tree), read-only and sandboxed to repoRoot.

tactical.explanation: readSource(repoRoot, relPath, line) resolves an absolute path via the pure guardPath domain guard (rejects ../ escapes — must stay inside repoRoot), then reads the file and returns a +/-8-line excerpt. Read-only; the read tools never write the filesystem.

anchors.note: node:fs read; repo-root sandbox (via guardPath); +/-8 line excerpt

nodes.label: repo source tree (repoRoot)
nodes.description: The recovered project's source directory (services.repoRoot). Every grounded read model (get_node, get_flow, the selected-nodes bundle) reads the actual source file behind each anchor from here, so Claude sees real code, not just a label. list_model and list_data_model never touch it.

tactical.explanation: For each anchor {path,line}, guardPath (domain/source/source-window.ts) resolves path.resolve(repoRoot, relPath) and rejects anything outside repoRoot + path.sep; source-gateway's readSource then reads the file and slices lines [line-8 .. line+8]. buildNodeContext calls it per anchor when includeSource is true (the default on the MCP path).

anchors.note: repoRoot sandbox guard against ../ escape

flows.name: A connected Claude reads grounded model context over the MCP read tools
flows.summary: A Claude session that registered the es-view MCP server pulls grounded domain context to ground a refactor. Over the streamable-HTTP /mcp transport it discovers ids with list_model, fetches a node with get_node, a whole flow (plus a Mermaid graph) with get_flow, the physical storage tree with list_data_model, and the human's curated set via the event-storming://selected-nodes resource. Every projection is served from the SAME in-memory state driven by the human: the merged model (agg-model, resolved once at boot) and the curated bundle (agg-context-bundle). The grounded reads (get_node/get_flow/bundle) pull REAL source excerpts from the repo filesystem behind each anchor; list_model/list_data_model stay pure in-memory. Nothing is written: this is the pure-read half of the bridge (the selection-aware get_current_selection is a sibling flow).
flows.trigger: A connected Claude session (registered via `claude mcp add`, initialized over POST /mcp) calls get_node / get_flow / list_model / list_data_model, or reads the `event-storming://selected-nodes` resource.

hotspots.label: Read-tool registered descriptions drift from actual behavior / mcp.md
hotspots.description: Two read tools advertise themselves inaccurately to a client selecting tools by description. get_flow's registered description lists 'trigger/summary, the command→aggregate→event chain, hotspots, and every node with its source anchors' but never mentions the Mermaid graph it returns — a feature mcp.md DOES document. list_data_model's registered description is relational-only ('servers ▸ databases ▸ tables ▸ columns') while the implementation (dataModelTree/renderDataModelMarkdown) is storage-neutral and mcp.md hedges with '(or the equivalent for non-relational storage)'. Human question: should the registered tool descriptions be regenerated from mcp.md/the implementation so a client picking tools by description isn't misled (get_flow yields a graph; list_data_model handles any storeKind)?

tactical.explanation: get_flow registerTool description (mcp-server.ts:57) omits Mermaid, yet renderFlowMarkdown appends fc.mermaid built by flowMermaid. list_data_model registerTool description (mcp-server.ts:77) says 'servers ▸ databases ▸ tables ▸ columns', but renderDataModelMarkdown labels each node by its freeform storeKind and walks any containment tree. mcp.md is the corrected face (mentions the Mermaid graph and the non-relational equivalent); the in-code tool descriptions were not kept in sync by the refactor.

anchors.note: description omits the Mermaid graph it returns
relational-only wording vs storage-neutral impl
appends the Mermaid graph to every get_flow result

hotspots.label: Grounded read results inline source for every node with no size cap
hotspots.description: get_flow grounds EVERY node in a flow and the selected-nodes resource grounds EVERY bundled item, each anchor carrying a ±8-line fenced source excerpt (includeSource defaults true on the MCP path). There is no cap on how large the returned markdown gets, even though the inbound request body is capped at 4MB. A large flow or a big curated bundle could return a very large tool result and eat the client's context window. Human question: should get_flow / the bundle resource cap or paginate grounded output, or expose an includeSource=false toggle on the MCP path (buildNodeContext already supports the flag, but the tools always pass the default)?

tactical.explanation: buildNodeContext({ includeSource = true }) reads a source excerpt per anchor; buildFlowContext and renderBundleMarkdown call it for every node/item and never pass includeSource:false. The MCP tools expose no way to opt out. Contrast: readJsonBody caps the INBOUND body at 4_000_000 bytes, but nothing bounds the OUTBOUND grounded markdown.

anchors.note: grounds every node with source (includeSource default true)
readSource excerpt per anchor, no cap
4MB cap on inbound body only; no outbound cap
